claims.text: Traditional EAM reference potentials cannot capture the full spectrum of atomic configurations in high-entropy alloys.
TOR-TILD's EAM reference potentials exhibit significant thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
A deep neural-network potential should be trained on diverse ab initio configurations from both solid and liquid high-entropy alloys.
The training dataset should represent configurations at temperatures near the alloys' melting points.
A deep-learning potential trained on representative solid and liquid configurations will faithfully interpolate among those configurations.
Faithful interpolation by the deep-learning potential will enhance phase-space overlap between the reference simulation and the ab initio target.
Training on broad and representative ab initio data enables a neural-network potential to model energies accurately across diverse solid and liquid configurations.
Training on broad and representative ab initio data enables a neural-network potential to model atomic forces accurately across diverse solid and liquid configurations.
Improved fidelity to the ab initio energy landscape reduces thermodynamic-integration path discrepancy relative to conventional EAM potentials.
The proposed deep-learning potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 50% or more relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Free-energy estimates obtained using the proposed potential will align more closely with direct ab initio molecular-dynamics results than estimates obtained using EAM references.
The proposed method applies to multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states near their melting temperatures.
Performance may deteriorate for alloy compositions lying substantially outside the training-data composition range.
Performance may deteriorate at temperatures far outside the training-data regime near melting.
The magnitude of mismatch reduction depends on the quality and representativeness of the training data.
Failure to achieve at least a 50% mismatch reduction relative to EAM references would falsify the hypothesis.
A significant deviation of the integrated free energy from a direct ab initio benchmark would falsify the hypothesis.
